identificationModule.briefTitle: Double Trigger in Patients With Low Number of Oocytes Retrieved Per Number of Preovulatory Follicles
identificationModule.officialTitle: Double Trigger in Patients With Low Number of Oocytes Retrieved Per Number of Preovulatory Follicles. A Randomized Controlled Trial

leadSponsor.name: Riyadh Fertility and Reproductive Health center

descriptionModule.briefSummary: The aim of this randomized controlled trial is to determine whether co-administration of GnRH agonist and hCG for final oocyte maturation ( 40 and 34 h prior to oocyte retrieval , respectively) can increase the oocytes yield in patients with history of poor oocytes yield, despite normal response to COH, due to low (\<50%) number of oocytes retrieved per number of follicles \> 14 mm in diameter on day of hCG administration

armGroups.label: Double trigger
armGroups.description: GnRH-agonist and HCG are used to trigger ovulation

armGroups.label: HCG
armGroups.description: HCG is used to trigger ovulation

interventions.name: Double trigger
interventions.description: Final follicular maturation is triggered by the co-administration of GnRH-agonist (Triptorelin acetate, decapeptyl 0.2 mg, Slough, United Kingdom) and 10000 IU of HCG, 40 and 34 h prior to oocyte retrieval, respectively

interventions.name: HCG trigger
interventions.description: Final follicular maturation is triggered by a dose of 10000 IU of HCG 36 h prior to oocyte retrieval

secondaryOutcomes.description: The presence of gestational sac detected by ultrasound examination

eligibilityModule.eligibilityCriteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Patients with history of poor oocytes yield in previous IVF attempt, despite normal response to COH, due to low (\<50%) number of oocytes retrieved per number of follicles \> 14 mm in diameter on day of hCG administration
* Patients with 6 to 15 mature follicles on the day oocyte trigger in the current IVF-ET attempt

Exclusion Criteria:

* Endometriosis
* PCOS

locations.facility: Riyadh Fertility and Reproductive Health center
